extracted.intended_audience: senior intelligence community officials, federal agency procurement policymakers, and OMB staff involved in implementation of OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rationale for applying (or seeking exemption from) OMB Circular A-76 when deciding whether government activities should be performed in-house or contracted out—with emphasis on protecting sensitive intelligence sources, methods, and mission requirements. The document discusses policy constraints, an illustrative DOE contracting incident, and recommends community-wide exemption procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: General A-76 policy — use of private sector when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 endorses relying on the private sector to provide goods and services whenever practical, economical, and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The circular's general policy favors contracting out commercial activities unless there is a clear justification for in-house performance. The memorandum affirms endorsement of these general policies while noting limits when sensitive intelligence material is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using strike risk as justification for in-house operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular states that activities may not be justified for in-house operation on the basis that there is a possibility of a strike by contract employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies cannot retain activities in-house solely because contracting employees might strike; this explicit A-76 rule removes 'strike risk' as a permissible reason to avoid contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using classified-program involvement as justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular states that activities may not be justified for in-house operation on the basis that the activity involves or supports a classified program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under current A-76 language, involvement with classified programs is not an allowable justification to keep an activity in-house, creating tension for intelligence organizations that must protect sources and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 does not recognize security protection as a basis for in-house operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft/revised A-76 did not change the policy that security reasons (including protection of intelligence sources and methods) do not justify in-house operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum argues that because A-76 does not accept security as a justification, agencies with sensitive missions cannot reconcile the circular with the need to protect intelligence material and therefore should seek relief or exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational impact and user acceptance must be considered when contracting sensitive services
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting operation of sensitive facilities (example: DOE's proposed contracting of an all-source communications center) can be unacceptable to users who rely on the facility and may refuse to cooperate if contractors operate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before contracting out functions that support intelligence dissemination or sensitive operations, agencies must evaluate whether users (other agencies, intelligence consumers) will accept contractor operation and the risk that they may cease transmissions or participation, undermining mission effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek community-wide exemption to protect sources and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Because responsibilities for protecting intelligence sources and methods are shared across the Intelligence Community, the memorandum recommends pursuing a consistent community-wide position seeking exemption from A-76 for sensitive activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended course is coordinated advocacy with OMB/other authorities to obtain relief from A-76 requirements where they conflict with intelligence security needs; the memorandum offers NSA staff support for this effort and requests DCI support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precedent and formal communications with OMB to decline participation
rubrics_metrics.description: CIA previously sent a formal letter (Oct 27, 1978) to OMB describing why it could not comply with A-76, and as a result CIA has not been participating in the A-76 program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting agency-specific rationales to OMB and seeking formal non-participation (via written explanation) is a procedural approach to avoid implementation where A-76 conflicts with mission requirements; other intelligence entities remain subject but could use similar rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 revision process addressed congressional concerns but not security exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the recent revision of the circular made provisions to accommodate congressional concerns about unlimited contract operation of certain services, it did not alter the policy barring justification for in-house operation on the basis of strike possibility or classified program involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy changes in the revision were limited; agencies should not assume the revised circular provides new security-related exemptions and must instead pursue other avenues (e.g., community-wide exemption requests) to address intelligence-specific needs.
